chunks: And from him (Al-Shaykh) from Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, and Muhammad ibn Isma'il, from al-Fadl ibn Shadhan, from Hammad ibn Isa, from Ibrahim ibn Umar al-Yamani, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him): that he was asked about a man who set out in

the months of Hajj performing Umrah, then he returned to his country. He (peace be upon him) said: 'There is no harm, and if he performed Hajj once in that year and performed Hajj individually (Hajj al-Frad), there is no blood-offering (dam) upon him. And indeed, al-Husayn ibn Ali (peace be upon him) set out on the Day of Tarwiyah to Iraq, and he had entered performing Umrah.'

key_terms.أَشْهُرِ الْحَجِّ: Months of Hajj (Shawwal, Dhu al-Qi'dah, and first 10 days of Dhu al-Hijjah)
key_terms.يَوْمَ التَّرْوِيَةِ: The Day of Tarwiyah (8th of Dhu al-Hijjah)

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling for someone who performs Umrah in the Hajj months and then returns home without performing Hajj immediately?
ai.summary: This ruling from Shaykh al-Tusi’s *Tahdhib* clarifies that performing Umrah during the Hajj months does not incur a penalty (dam) if one subsequently performs Hajj individually in the same year, a principle supported by the precedent of Imam al-Husayn (AS) who performed Umrah before departing for Iraq. This narration highlights the flexibility in Shia jurisprudence regarding the combination of rituals and underscores the continuity of prophetic practice through the Ahl al-Bayt. The reference to al-Husayn’s journey serves not only as a legal analogy but also as a spiritual link between the minor pilgrimage and the ultimate sacrifice of Karbala.
